gaps.construct: heap holds items of any type that supports <
gaps.description: The doc shows a type parameter only on a type declaration (Queue of T); there is no way for an operation to introduce T or to bound it by an ordering, so 'where T is Ordered' is invented.

gaps.construct: newitem < parent dispatches to the items' __lt__
gaps.description: Comparison of user values relies on an ordering capability the doc never names; 'is less than' is only shown on Int.
No shift operator; replaced by (current - 1) / 2, which equals the shift for non-negative values.

gaps.construct: rebinding the parameter pos inside the loop
gaps.description: The doc never shows a parameter being set, so a var copy 'current' is introduced and the original name is lost in the loop.
The doc has 'item i of items' as an expression and 'set field of record to', but never sets a list element; 'set item current of heap to parent' is assumed.

gaps.construct: implicit IndexError from heap[pos] when pos is out of range
gaps.description: The doc does not say what an out-of-range 'item i of items' does (proof obligation, failure, or abort), so the failure behaviour is left unstated.

gaps.construct: three positional parameters with no label words
gaps.description: Every doc header with more than one parameter uses label words (from, in, onto, for, with); whether 'to siftdown heap startpos pos' is valid is not stated.

invented_syntax: given heap is an editable List of T where T is Ordered
set item current of heap to parent
notes: Python's 'continue then break' maps directly onto skip and stop, and the required decreases line is easy to supply. The function is short but typical of the standard library: it is generic over an ordering, and the doc has no way to say that. List element mutation is used constantly in real code and needs an explicit example.
